t: A low-cost ECP5 FPGA board that can boot Linux on a homemade RISC-V processor.
steps: Buy the iCESugar-Pro from MuseLab on Tindie for about 60 US dollars.
Plug the module into the Ext-Board and fit the included headers.
Connect the included USB-C cable to your computer.
Drag the ready blink bitstream from the repo onto the iCELink drive and watch the LED.
Install the YosysHQ OSS CAD Suite on Linux or on Windows through WSL2.
Build the blink example yourself and load it with icesprog.
Try the UART and HDMI demos next.
meta: Open Board. From $60. A few stores.
